reviews.one_line_contribution: A number with an interval: how much an ALFWorld procedural memory bank is still worth once a reflective search optimizer has written the instruction from the *same* training episodes, measured at the bank's own re-tuned retrieval budget and game-paired against a second instruction optimized from *disjoint* episodes of the same distribution and titrated to the same no-memory accuracy, the pair of residuals being offered as an identification of episode-specific vs distribution-level absorption.
reviews.closest_prior_work: ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144, verified to exist) is the real threat, and the proposal concedes it: its ALFWorld ablation already reports full 59 / retrieve-only 55 / insights-only 50, i.e. each container alone recovers 85-93% of the pair built from one training pool. EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202, verified; it does run GEPA and ReasoningBank as comparable self-evolution artifacts) supplies the second half. What survives is real but thin: the instruction container is a search optimizer rather than an extraction routine, k is re-tuned per instruction, and the disjoint-episode level match is an identification device I could not find published. The reason this still threatens the paper is the proposal's own pre-registered branch structure: in the E-and-not-D branch the conclusion is 'any instruction optimized on this distribution already holds the bank's value, practical conclusion unchanged', which is ExpeL's qualitative finding with a confidence interval attached. Only the E-and-D branch buys something ExpeL does not have, and by the proposal's own power analysis (D thresholded at 3pt with an MDE of 4pt) that branch is roughly a coin flip even if the hypothesis is exactly true.
reviews.strongest_objection: Every primary quantity is computed downstream of an argmax on S_dev, and the resulting selection bias is larger than the effect the primaries are trying to bound. (1) k*(I) is the k in {1,3,5,7} maximizing the paired gain of B over M0 on 75 games per k. On 75 paired games the SE of a paired gain is several points; taking the max over four values inflates g(I) at every instruction, and inflates it by *different* amounts at I0*, I_P and I'_match depending on how flat each k-curve is. The design then declares E only when |g-hat(I_P)| <= 0.9pt and tests D at a 3pt threshold - both finer than the bias just injected. (2) I'_match is itself selected: up to ten snapshots (r in {50,100,200,350,500} x 2 seeds, extendable to 750) are screened for an S_dev no-memory accuracy within 1.5pt of l_P. Selecting on a noisy dev estimate is a winner's curse: I'_match's *S_test* no-memory accuracy will regress away from l_P, so the level match that the design says makes 'headroom cancel by construction' does not hold on the test split, and row 3's D estimate re-imports the very headroom rival row 3 exists to exclude. Row 9, the null replicate, cannot catch either problem, because it re-uses the frozen k*(I_P) and a fixed instruction and therefore replicates decoding noise only. A secondary form of the same objection: matching I' to I_P on accuracy alone leaves them unmatched on rollout budget, length and prescriptiveness - the design token-matches the *scaffold* (I0_pad) and the *banks* (B', M_shuf) but never token-matches I'_match to I_P - so a positive D is equally well explained by 'the disjoint-episode instruction is shorter and less prescriptive, leaving more room for injected items' as by episode provenance.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Take every selection off the estimation split. Use the ~700-trial reserve as a selection-only partition: tune k and pick the I' snapshot there, and report the S_test primary at a pre-fixed k, or better, drop the argmax entirely and make the primary a comparison of full k-curves (g at k in {1,3,5,7} for I0*, I_P, I'_match) so the retrieval-budget re-tuning becomes a reported surface rather than a bias-generating choice. Re-measure I'_match's no-memory accuracy on S_test and enter the realized level gap as a covariate (or an explicit adjustment) in D rather than asserting cancellation. Token- and length-match I'_match to I_P, or additionally run I' at the identical 350-rollout budget and report D at both the level-matched and budget-matched instructions. Promote two arms out of Tier 1 into Tier 0: the compiled/extraction instruction C (this is what separates novelty claim (i) from ExpeL and AutoManual, and it is currently deferred) and the coupling arm I2 optimized with memory in context, which is the configuration deployed systems actually use and the question the research track asks. Finally, either abandon the +/-3pt TOST framing, since the design admits it is declarable only at |g-hat| <= 0.9pt, and report the interval as the result, or spend the reserve to reach n = 2400 up front rather than conditionally.
reviews.missing_baseline: The ExpeL retrieve-only container - raw retrieved training trajectories in the memory slot - is absent from the entire grid. On ALFWorld that is the *stronger* of ExpeL's two containers (55 vs 50 for insights-only), so the paper measures the residual of the weaker container only and a reviewer will ask whether the residual survives when the memory slot holds demonstrations rather than distilled INSIGHT/PROCEDURE items. This also matters because the track frames the composition as 'the optimizer owns instructions, memory owns the demonstration slot', which the design never instantiates. Second omission, equally demanded: an instruction produced by a cheap non-search extraction routine (AutoManual / AutoGuide / ACE-style compiled block) from the same 300 P_train episodes, run as an instruction arm in Tier 0. Without it the claim that a *search-based* optimizer is the new thing is untested - I_type and I0_pad are controls for label knowledge and length, not for extraction. Third, deferred rather than missing: I2 (optimized with B in context) and the joint arm J sit in Tier 1, so the plan measures decomposition but not coupling.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is above average for a proposal - dated scans, conceded collisions, a narrowly stated survivor, and four named open obligations - and I verified its factual spine rather than taking it on trust. Six searches confirmed that arXiv 2308.10144 (ExpeL), 2507.19457 (GEPA, ICLR 2026 oral), 2509.25140 (ReasoningBank), 2607.05202 (EvoAgentBench, which does compare GEPA and ReasoningBank artifacts), 2604.14585 (Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip, ICML 2026 workshop; the 49%-below-zero-shot figure on Claude Haiku is as quoted) and 2607.28272 (MemHarness; raw injection 70.1 vs 76.4 for RL without memory on ALFWorld, exactly as quoted) all exist and say what the proposal says they say. I found no preprint measuring the residual of a memory bank at a search-optimized, same-episode instruction, and none using an episode-disjoint, level-matched instruction as an identification device; on the searches I ran, the surviving contribution is not scooped. Three weaknesses in the check itself. (a) It missed adjacent 2026 work sitting on exactly this seam: arXiv 2603.21520 (Generalizable Self-Evolving Memory for Automatic Prompt Optimization, memory driving the optimizer), arXiv 2606.00619 (MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs, which explicitly argues prompt-level optimization is insufficient to substitute for memory-system evolution - the direct thematic counterparty to this proposal's thesis and unaddressed by it), and arXiv 2606.23664 (MAS-PromptBench: When Does Prompt Optimization Improve Multi-Agent LLM Systems?). None is a hard collision, but three uncited papers on the seam means the scan was not as complete as its framing implies. (b) The check reports that the abstracts of arXiv 2604.18206 and 2604.11811 were unretrievable from its node and lists them as unread; 2604.18206 (A Control Architecture for Training-Free Memory Use) was reachable from my node, so this is a node limitation being reported as a literature fact, and an unread paper about when memory should be exposed or retired is precisely the one that could pre-empt the re-tuned-budget half of the survivor. (c) The proposal's own open obligation (1), the provenance / held-out-episode crossover in the prompt-optimization, contamination and data-attribution literatures, is the obligation that could still kill the identification claim, and it remains unrun; my six searches did not close it either. From my own memory and unverified by search: matched-performance, same-example-vs-different-example designs are standard in the memorization-versus-generalization and data-attribution literature, so 'nobody has done this' is more likely to fail on transfer-of-a-known-design grounds than on agent-memory grounds, and the proposal has not looked there. Net: no collision found, novelty not scooped, but the check has not yet earned the word 'novel' for the identification device.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A paired, pre-registered ALFWorld measurement of how much a procedural memory bank is still worth once a reflective prompt optimizer has written the instruction from the identical training episodes (the 'residual' g(I_P)), plus a task-disjoint, no-memory-accuracy-matched instruction I'_match intended to separate episode-specific absorption from distribution-level absorption.
reviews.closest_prior_work: ExpeL (2308.10144) and EvoAgentBench (2607.05202), and ExpeL is the more dangerous of the two because the proposal quotes it correctly against itself. I verified ExpeL's ALFWorld ablation: full 59, retrieve-only 55, insights-only 50. The proposal's estimand g(I) = acc(I x B) - acc(I x M0) is, in ExpeL's own table, 59 - 50 = 9 points: the residual value of the retrieval container measured at an already-written insights instruction built from the same training pool. So the joint cell the proposal calls unpublished is published, and its published value is about +9pt, not about 0. The entire paper is a bet that swapping ExpeL's extraction routine for a search-based optimizer closes a 9-point gap. That bet is placed with a 350-rollout GEPA-lite budget on 300 training games (one full sweep plus 50 rollouts, i.e. roughly one mutation actually evaluated) and a local 27B/32B reflector, which is the weakest possible version of the very mechanism the novelty rests on. EvoAgentBench compounds this: it already puts a bank method and GEPA on a shared trajectory pool with a held-out split explicitly constructed so test tasks do not duplicate training instances, which is already a provenance-controlled instruction-vs-bank comparison. The proposal's genuine increment over these two is narrow: the joint cell measured with per-instruction re-tuned k, and the disjoint-pool level-matched arm. That is a delta on a conceded result, and the proposal says so itself ('Novelty is capped by the concessions above').
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory family is arithmetically unlikely to declare anything, and the proposal proves this in its own text. E (equivalence within +/-3pt) is declarable only when |g-hat(I_P)| <= 0.9pt, because SE(g) ~ 1.25pt at n=1800 with DEFF 1.4. D is thresholded at 3pt but powered at ~4pt, so 'a true 3pt difference passes about half the time' (their Risk Factor 3). The prior evidence the proposal itself assembles - ExpeL's ~9pt analogous residual, this program's own +0.6 to +2.4pt, MemHarness's raw-injection gap - all point to a true residual in the 1-4pt band, which is exactly the band where E cannot be declared and superiority cannot be claimed either. The modal outcome of row 2 crossed with row 3 is therefore 'bounded residual, D indeterminate': two confidence intervals and no claim, dressed as a pre-registered reading. Second, and independent of power, row 3 does not identify what it claims. I'_match is a mid-run snapshot of an optimizer run on P'_train, titrated only on no-memory S_dev accuracy. Matching accuracy does not match instruction maturity, specificity, or length, and the design token-matches I0_pad to I_P but never token- or budget-matches I'_match to I_P. A larger g at I'_match is therefore fully explained by 'I' is an earlier, thinner, less specific instruction that leaves more for the bank to say' - a rival the proposal never names and never arms. Since D is the one arm carrying the word 'episode-specific' in the title, an identification hole there is not a secondary blemish. Third, the bank B is an insight/strategy bank (ExpeL-style INSIGHT/PROCEDURE/OUTCOME or ReasoningBank-style strategies), not a raw-trajectory retrieval bank, and ExpeL found retrieval (55) beat insights (50) on ALFWorld specifically because ALFWorld rewards concrete action sequences. The design therefore measures the residual of the container ALFWorld is known to reward less, which biases the whole study toward the null it hopes to declare.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Change the primary estimand. Make the retention ratio R = g(I_P)/g(I0*) with a cluster-bootstrap CI the confirmatory quantity instead of a TOST that only fires below 0.9pt; R is always declarable, is the quantity Experience Distillation reports, and answers the title's question in the form readers want. If the TOST is kept, either raise rows 2-3 to n >= 3000 (the ~700 reserve is not enough) or pre-justify a +/-5pt margin from a stated decision-theoretic cost rather than picking 3. (2) Add row 3b: an early snapshot of I_P itself, from the SAME episodes, titrated to the same no-memory level and matched on rollout budget and token count to I'_match. Without it, D confounds episode provenance with optimizer maturity, and D is the title. (3) Add a raw-trajectory demonstration-retrieval bank at I_P (see missing_baseline) so the null is not declared on the weaker container. (4) Give the optimizer a budget that makes 'search-based reflective optimizer' true: 350 rollouts over 300 games is one sweep plus 50, and calling coverage '100% by construction' is definitional, not empirical. Several thousand rollouts, or a candidate-count-per-generation table, or stop claiming search is the differentiator from AutoManual/AutoGuide. (5) Move official valid_unseen from Tier 1 into Tier 0. A claim about ALFWorld memory that never touches the split every cited memory paper reports on, and that sits behind contingency cuts, will not be read as on the published axis. (6) Close collision obligation (1) and read 2608.14036 before freezing, not after.
reviews.missing_baseline: A raw-trajectory / demonstration-retrieval memory bank at I_P, k- and token-matched to B. Every arm in the grid uses a distilled insight-or-strategy bank, but ExpeL's ALFWorld ablation (which the proposal quotes) shows retrieve-only 55 versus insights-only 50, i.e. the trajectory container is the stronger one in exactly this environment, and MIPROv2 - also cited - frames the whole instruction-versus-demonstration decomposition around demonstrations, not distilled prose. Declaring 'the optimized instruction absorbed the bank' after testing only the prose-shaped bank tests the arm most similar to the instruction and is close to circular; a reviewer will read the null as an artifact of container choice. Second omission, equally demandable: a same-episode, budget- and level-matched early snapshot of I_P as the comparator for I'_match, so that D contrasts episode provenance rather than optimizer maturity. Third, minor: no scaffold-plus-random-instruction control distinguishes 'an optimized instruction' from 'any long task-specific instruction'; I0_pad pads with task-neutral prose only.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually honest for this venue and concedes six lines of prior work by name, which is credit due. It is also, by its own text, incomplete: obligation (1) - the provenance / held-out-episode crossover search - was run once, found nothing, and is called 'not sufficient'; two 2026 IDs are cited unread; and the appendix of 2608.14036 is deferred. By the standard that an unsearched claim of novelty is a weakness, this one is partly self-reported as unestablished. I ran six searches. VERIFIED AS REAL AND AS DESCRIBED: 2308.10144 ExpeL, and its ALFWorld ablation numbers 59 / 55 / 50 (arxiv.org/abs/2308.10144); 2604.14585 'Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip: Diagnosing When It Helps in Compound AI Systems', ICML 2026 workshop, 49% of runs below zero-shot confirmed (arxiv.org/abs/2604.14585); 2607.28272 MemHarness, ALFWorld raw injection 70.1 and RL baseline 76.4 both confirmed (arxiv.org/abs/2607.28272); 2606.29914 MemDelta exists (arxiv.org/abs/2606.29914) but its one-variable flip is demonstrated on LongMemEval-S, not on ALFWorld, so it supports the methodology point and not the environment choice; 2511.21730 exists as 'A Benchmark for Procedural Memory Retrieval in Language Agents' (arxiv.org/abs/2511.21730); 2608.14036 exists as 'Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't' (arxiv.org/html/2608.14036v1). PARTIALLY VERIFIED: 2607.05202 EvoAgentBench exists (arxiv.org/abs/2607.05202, 6 Jul 2026, four domains, ability graphs, held-out tasks that do not duplicate training instances), but the returned description gives 1,006 train / 367 test tasks, and I could not confirm the proposal's '528/267 trajectories on Qwen3.5-27B' or the ReasoningBank +3.6 / GEPA +1.2 figures; the authors should cite the exact table. NO DIRECT COLLISION FOUND on the surviving contribution as stated (residual of a bank at a search-optimized same-episode instruction, with a disjoint-episode level-matched control) - the searches surfaced no paper making that claim. NEW ADJACENT ITEMS THE PROPOSAL DOES NOT CITE, all surfaced by these searches: arxiv.org/html/2609.00549 'Skill Following: Evaluating Actual Skill Use in Retrieval-Enabled LLM Agents' (Sep 2026), which collides directly with rival (e)'s instrument - the item-following rate f(I) is that paper's estimand, and it must now be cited and its metric adopted or distinguished; arxiv.org/abs/2606.00619 MemPro (memory pipeline as an evolvable program, i.e. optimizer applied to the memory side); arxiv.org/abs/2606.23127 'Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents' / AFTER, which holds task-skill annotations fixed to separate skill quality from retrieval quality; arxiv.org/html/2608.09096 'Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?'; arxiv.org/pdf/2603.21520 'Generalizable Self-Evolving Memory for Automatic Prompt Optimization'. None of these is a clean scoop, so the collision check does not sink the paper - but the residual novelty after ExpeL's own 9-point joint-cell number and EvoAgentBench's shared-trajectory table is thin enough that 2609.00549 and 2608.14036 must be read before any freeze; if 2608.14036's appendix contains the token-matched compiled-block comparison the proposal suspects, the contribution shrinks to the ALFWorld measurement with its controls, which is the outcome the proposal already anticipates in writing.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered ALFWorld measurement of the residual value of a procedural memory bank once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA-lite) has written an instruction from the identical training episodes, with an episode-disjoint, no-memory-accuracy-matched instruction as the control that is meant to separate 'the instruction absorbed these episodes' from 'the instruction learned this distribution'. The proposal is honest that the qualitative result is already published and that the contribution is an interval plus an identification arm on top of it; I can state the contribution, but it is a measurement, not a claim.
reviews.closest_prior_work: ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144), which the proposal concedes. I verified the paper exists and that its ALFWorld ablation does compare full / retrieve-only / insights-only and concludes the two containers are 'essential and synergistic' with retrieval mattering more on ALFWorld; the specific 59/55/50 numbers were not visible in the returned snippets, so the load-bearing framing number is unverified from this node. ExpeL threatens novelty because it already establishes container redundancy on the same benchmark from one training pool, and 85-93% single-container recovery is close enough to 'residual is small' that a reviewer will ask what the interval buys. It does NOT fully threaten, because ExpeL's insight block is a fixed extraction routine at a fixed retrieval budget, not a search-based optimizer with per-instruction re-tuned k, and ExpeL has no episode-disjoint level-matched arm. EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202) is the second threat and is the weaker concession than the proposal implies: the ID exists, but the returned abstract describes web research, algorithmic reasoning, software engineering and knowledge work via Ability Graphs, with no ALFWorld and no confirmation of the '528/267 trajectories on Qwen3.5-27B, ReasoningBank +3.6, GEPA +1.2' table the proposal quotes. So the claim 'an optimizer given the same episodes gets roughly what a bank gets is also published' is currently an out-of-domain extrapolation the proposal presents as settled.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory family is arithmetically unlikely to ever fire, and every pre-registered fallback lands on a restatement of ExpeL. By the proposal's own numbers, E (equivalence within +/-3pt) is declarable only when |g-hat(I_P)| <= 0.9pt, and D is powered at ~4pt while thresholded at 3pt, so the intersection E AND D that licenses the title has low probability even under the authors' own planning assumptions; the modal outcome is a 'bounded residual' in (0.9, 3] plus 'distribution-level absorption', i.e. 37,600 episodes to say what ExpeL's ablation table already says qualitatively. Compounding this, D is confounded in a way no arm removes: I'_match is an EARLY SNAPSHOT (r in {50,100,200,350,500}) of a longer run, matched to I_P only on no-memory S_dev accuracy. Matching accuracy does not match optimization degree or instruction specificity, so g(I'_match) > g(I_P) is equally well explained by 'I_P is a converged, densely specified instruction that crowds the context and I' is an undercooked one' as by 'I_P absorbed these particular episodes'. Row 6 (I0_pad) controls length but not specificity, and the row-3/row-2 contrast is the paper's only identification. Two further defects make the primaries fragile at the 3pt scale they are decided at: (i) row 9 is labelled the treatment-free null replicate but it is I_P x {M0, B} at seed 37, which is the SAME treatment contrast at a different decoding seed, so pooling it into the 'null floor' contaminates the null with the real effect and makes the 95th-percentile floor rise exactly when memory works; (ii) k*(I) is chosen per instruction by maximizing paired gain over k in {1,3,5,7} at 75 games per k, where the SE of a paired gain is roughly 5-6pt, so the 'bank's own re-tuned retrieval budget' - contribution (ii) in the Related Work - is selected essentially at random, and independent noisy k-selections for I_P and I'_match feed straight into D's 3pt threshold. The agent-model and bank-format screening is worse: a 5pt threshold judged on 50 games picks the whole downstream stack on noise, and G1's subsequent 5pt requirement is then evaluated on the winner of that selection.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Fix the null: make row 9 a genuine treatment-free replicate (I_P x M0 at two decoding seeds, and B x B at two seeds), and stop pooling a live treatment contrast into the null floor. 2) Fix the power problem rather than pre-registering around it: the reserve (~700 trials) should go into rows 2-3 up front, and the margin should be set from the measured S_dev SE, not planned at +/-3pt when the design can only declare 0.9pt; alternatively drop TOST and make the retention ratio R = g(I_P)/g(I0*) with a CI the PRIMARY endpoint, which is estimable at this n and is the quantity practitioners actually want. 3) De-confound D: match I'_match to I_P on optimizer budget AND on instruction token count and rule count, not only on no-memory accuracy, and add the symmetric arm - I_P evaluated against B' vs B is row 4, but the missing mirror is I'_match x B' (its own-episode bank), which turns a one-sided comparison into a 2x2 provenance design where the interaction, not a difference of differences across unmatched instructions, is the estimand. 4) Move k*(I) selection to a sample size where it means something (all 300 S_dev games per k, or a single shared k with the k-curve reported as the sensitivity analysis), or pre-register k as fixed and report re-tuning as secondary. 5) Add an upper-bound memory arm (gold trajectory of the exact test task injected at I_P) so that g(I_P) ~ 0 can be distinguished from 'the I_P prompt does not read the memory slot at all'; the item-following rate f(I) is an action-string heuristic that any accuracy change perturbs and cannot carry that load alone. 6) Verify and quote EvoAgentBench's actual table, or drop it as a concession; the argument currently leans on an out-of-domain benchmark whose numbers were not readable from this node.
reviews.missing_baseline: The static demonstration container from the same episodes, at Tier 0. The paper's claim is 'the bank is worth nothing once the instruction has seen these episodes', but the only memory-slot contents in the Tier-0 grid are the retrieved bank B, its provenance variants (B', B^on) and a random-item control. A reviewer will demand I_P x C (the token-matched compiled block from B) and a MIPROv2-style bootstrapped k-shot demonstration set drawn from P_train with the retriever removed - both currently relegated to Tier 1. Without them the design cannot separate 'retrieval adds nothing over an optimized instruction' from 'this particular distilled bank adds nothing', which is the difference between a claim about memory systems and a claim about one bank. Second omission, and the one the research-track brief actually asks for: the coupling arm I2 (instruction optimized WITH the bank in context) x {B, M0} is the deployment configuration every framework in the related work ships, and it is also Tier 1; a proposal titled around whether memory is an un-optimized prompt that never runs the co-optimized condition in its main grid has skipped the composition the track posed. Third: no bank-size scaling arm (B at 150/300/600 episodes), so a null residual at 300 episodes cannot be distinguished from a bank that is simply too small.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually candid - it names its own conceded collisions and lists four unrun obligations - but it is by its own admission incomplete, and obligation (1), the provenance / held-out-episode crossover search, is the one the author states would reduce the contribution to 'the ALFWorld measurement with its controls'. One query run and nothing found is not a search. Under this venue's standard that is a weakness, not a neutral. My own six searches: VERIFIED EXISTS AND SAYS WHAT THE PROPOSAL SAYS - arXiv 2604.14585 'Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip: Diagnosing When It Helps in Compound AI Systems' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14585), 72 runs, 49% below zero-shot on Claude Haiku, ICML 2026 workshop; arXiv 2507.19457 GEPA, confirmed ICLR 2026 Oral; arXiv 2308.10144 ExpeL, ALFWorld full vs retrieve-only vs insights-only ablation confirmed qualitatively, exact 59/55/50 values NOT confirmed in returned snippets; arXiv 2607.28272 'MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28272) exists, ALFWorld + WebShop, headline 85.2% ALFWorld, the quoted 70.1 vs 76.4 baseline pair not visible in snippets. PARTIALLY VERIFIED - arXiv 2607.05202 EvoAgentBench exists (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05202) but the returned abstract covers web research, algorithmic reasoning, software engineering and knowledge work via Ability Graphs, with no ALFWorld and no sign of the ReasoningBank +3.6 / GEPA +1.2 / 528-267 / Qwen3.5-27B table the proposal quotes as its central 'already published' concession. NO DIRECT COLLISION FOUND: two collision-targeted searches returned nothing that measures a memory bank's residual value at a search-optimized instruction built from the same episodes, and nothing with an episode-disjoint level-matched instruction control. NEAR MISSES THE CHECK DOES NOT LIST, all surfaced by my searches and all 2026: arXiv 2603.21520 'Generalizable Self-Evolving Memory for Automatic Prompt Optimization' (MemAPO), which reconceptualizes prompt optimization itself as accumulated experience with a dual success/error memory - this is the strongest unlisted adjacency, because it directly asserts the containers are the same object, and if its evaluation includes an instruction-vs-memory decomposition it collides with the framing if not the number; arXiv 2606.03083 DeltaMem, which stores experience as residual deltas to cut cross-episode redundancy and reports leading both ALFWorld splits with per-component ablations; arXiv 2603.12631 'Joint Optimization of Multi-agent Memory System'; arXiv 2608.04761 InsightEmb. None of these is a kill, so I did not move novelty down for a collision - but I did not move it up either, because the surviving contribution as stated ('an interval on top of an accepted qualitative result') is small, the author agrees it is small, and the unrun obligation (1) could still shrink it further. Anything I believe about pre-2026 memory-as-instruction work beyond these results is from my own memory and unverified.
